1.finding: Basic = diluted EPS Rs 16.13 on PAT to owners Rs 10,677.74 cr = 661.84 crore shares, the share count after the Aug-2026 split of Rs 1,000 shares into Rs 2 shares (applied retrospectively). Pure OFS: no new shares.

2.finding: CFO Rs 6,325.58 / 7,704.96 / 12,477.53 cr FY24-26 against PAT Rs 11,841.55 / 10,825.12 / 10,698.12 cr: cumulative 80% of PAT. FY24-25 CFO was held down by a build-up of deposits under the mine-closure plan and receivables; H1 FY27 CFO Rs 8,997.13 cr is 1.8x PAT.

3.finding: Current tax Rs 3,466.16 / 3,406.60 / 3,401.66 cr = 22-24% of PBT; profit is taxed in cash.

4.finding: Executives are seconded from Coal India and the company pays CIL for shared services; full related-party tables not compiled in this run.

5.finding: Pure offer for sale by Coal India: the company receives no proceeds.

7.finding: No goodwill; the business was built, not bought.

8.finding: Top customer (NTPC) 14.64%, top 5 41.09%, top 10 55.94% of FY26 revenue, all on long-term fuel supply agreements; state and central power utilities 44.81% of revenue. Typical of Indian coal.

9.finding: Contingent liabilities Rs 12,513.29 cr at Sep-26 (55.86% of net worth), up from Rs 8,506.23 cr at Mar-26 mainly on income-tax demands (Rs 8,074.83 cr). Delayed receivables from APGENCO Rs 1,929.88 cr and APPDCL Rs 502.16 cr.

R1.finding: Unmodified opinion (Kadmawala & Co, appointed by the C&AG) with emphasis of matter and other matters: no insurance on assets; Rs 76.55 cr unplanned depreciation flagged by the C&AG; labour codes. Separately, the board has no independent directors at the RHP date (the Ministry of Coal appoints directors); the company has sought SEBI exemptions from board and committee composition rules (p. 42). No qualification.

R2.finding: CARO remarks include reconciliation of MSME dues and of GST records; none rises to a qualification.

R3.finding: Pure offer for sale: no proceeds to the company, so no monitoring agency.

R4.finding: Mainboard issue; net offer QIB up to 50%, NII at least 15%, retail at least 35%; employee reservation 3,30,91,815 shares and CIL shareholder reservation 6,61,83,630 shares (10% of the offer).

R6.finding: SBI Capital, Axis, BOB Capital, IDBI Capital and IIFL: large managers with long PSU-disinvestment records; track record not compiled in this run.

rationale.g1: Revenue Rs 31,634.35 / 31,353.02 / 30,549.59 cr FY24-26 (-0.9%, -2.6%): FSA prices fell from Rs 1,438.40 to Rs 1,354.17 a tonne and e-auction premiums collapsed (pp. 511-512). H1 FY27 revenue +9.3% on higher dispatch (offtake 127% of production) though production fell 9% (pp. 88, 124-125). Coal demand grows 3-4% a year to FY31 per the CRISIL report commissioned by the company. Neutral 3-3.5%; Bear flat (no price rise, volumes stuck); Bull 6% fading to 4.5%.
rationale.m: Operating EBITDA margin 46.41% / 43.55% / 41.69% FY24-26 and 40.07% in H1 FY27 (p. 124). Revenue includes a non-cash reversal of the stripping-activity provision worth about 1.6% of revenue (pp. 511-512). Neutral 42% = three-year average 43.9% less that reversal; Bear 37% (wage revision and contractor costs keep rising, prices flat); Bull 45%.
rationale.nwc: Inventory + receivables - payables = 5.9% / 8.6% / 13.0% of revenue FY24-26 (receivable days 22 -> 41, p. 124). Neutral 11%; Bear 14% (state utility delays persist, p. 24); Bull 9%.
rationale.roic: RoACE 107% / 83% / 73% FY24-26 (p. 124). Terminal ROIC 25% (Neutral) is well below today's level because coal is a depleting resource facing an energy transition; Bear 15%, Bull 35%.
rationale.capex: D&A input set to FY26 capex of Rs 2,929.61 cr (book D&A Rs 1,632.27 cr), because capex has run at 2-4x book D&A for three years (Rs 3,839.80 / 2,907.52 / 2,929.61 cr, p. 124) to open and replace mines; FY26 revenue fell, so the toolkit's growth-capex term is nil and capex is modelled as D&A. Net debt = borrowings Rs 3.16 cr - cash Rs 1,846.82 cr - other bank balances Rs 13,281.39 cr - current investments Rs 960.26 cr at Mar-26 (pp. 86-87) = net cash Rs 16,085.31 cr. The mine-closure provision (Rs 1,344.42 cr) is covered by escrow deposits of Rs 1,986.75 cr held outside this cash (p. 384), so both are left out. Pure OFS: no proceeds credited.
rationale.wacc: House CAPM with two changes, both stated: size premium 0% (the issuer would list at about Rs 90,000 cr, a large cap) and target debt weight 0% (borrowings are nil and the company funds capex from cash). Cost of equity = WACC = 14.2%. Terminal growth 3.0% instead of 4.5%: coal is a finite, regulated commodity whose domestic demand is expected to plateau in the 2030s as renewables scale.
rationale.relative: Relative value on peer-median P/E only (P/B weight 0): MCL's RoNW of 54% is two to ten times the peers' 5-28%, so a peer P/B would mis-price it. Peers are the RHP's own set (p. 123); Bharat Coking Coal is excluded because its P/E is not meaningful (EPS Rs 0.28).
